title: A nonprofit director sits on the City panel that recommends its funding

beats.text: In SoMa, developers of new housing pay a fee into a fund,
the SoMa Community Stabilization Fund.
A seven-seat committee advises the City on how to spend it.

visual.label: Community Advisory Committee
visual.sub: seven seats; advises on how the fund is spent

beats.text: Since March 2020, one member has been Misha Olivas.

visual.label: Community Advisory Committee
visual.sub: seven seats; advises on how the fund is spent

beats.text: She also works for United Playaz, a SoMa nonprofit the fund pays.

visual.label: United Playaz
visual.sub: Director of Community and Family Engagement

beats.text: Every year, her disclosures list a salary over 100,000 dollars.

visual.label: United Playaz
visual.sub: Director of Community and Family Engagement

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: In October 2022, the committee recommended money for four building projects.

visual.label: 1044 Howard St
visual.sub: next door to the United Playaz clubhouse

beats.text: One was for United Playaz, to buy 1044 Howard Street. How much?

visual.label: 1044 Howard St
visual.sub: next door to the United Playaz clubhouse

beats.text: 1,115,470 dollars.

visual.label: SoMa Fund money recommended for United Playaz

beats.text: She’s paid by the group the money went to.

visual.line: members of advisory bodies must generally stay out of contract advice that affects an organization they are tied to

beats.text: The City Attorney has advised such members to stay out of decisions like this.

visual.line: members of advisory bodies must generally stay out of contract advice that affects an organization they are tied to

beats.text: Did she step aside? The minutes weren’t found.

visual.label: recusal notices on file; none from this committee

beats.text: And of 408 recusal notices on file, none comes from this committee.

visual.label: recusal notices on file; none from this committee

beats.text: To be clear: three City staff, not the committee, scored the bids.

visual.label: Scored by MOHCD staff
visual.sub: United Playaz scored highest of five bidders

beats.text: United Playaz scored highest.

visual.label: Scored by MOHCD staff
visual.sub: United Playaz scored highest of five bidders

beats.text: A second member was president of TODCO, a SoMa housing developer.

visual.label: TODCO
visual.sub: a SoMa housing developer; its president sat on the same committee

beats.text: Its return records 151,000 dollars to United Playaz, to support purchase of property.

visual.label: TODCO grant to United Playaz, year to June 2023

beats.text: Then the timing. The Assessor gives the building a sale date of December 7, 2022.
The Board voted the money on February 14, 2023, 11 to 0.
One reading: the sale closed first, so the Board voted on a done deal.
The recorder’s index has the deed to United Playaz recorded on December 7: 69 days before the vote.

visual.text: deed to United Playaz Inc recorded 2022-12-07 (document 2022109688)

beats.text: Same-day loans, one from the selling trust, point to a buyer closing on borrowed money, repaid by a grant later.

visual.text: deed to United Playaz Inc recorded 2022-12-07 (document 2022109688)

beats.text: Planned City money came to 3,115,470 dollars,
The expected cost: 2.16 million.
The rest was said to cover renovation.

visual.line: report the appraised value and final cost within 30 days of the purchase

beats.text: The Board wanted the appraisal and final price within 30 days. That report wasn’t found.

visual.line: report the appraised value and final cost within 30 days of the purchase

beats.text: In September 2026, the Ethics Commission fined another member,
Janetta Johnson, 600 dollars.
She had voted while disqualified.
And a Controller review of United Playaz, in fiscal 2021-22, had no findings.
The records don’t show whether Olivas voted. Or how much United Playaz paid.

cards: How much United Playaz paid for the building

beats.text: What would settle it? The committee’s minutes and roll calls. And the deed, which would show the price.

cards.what: Committee minutes and roll calls, October 20, 2022
The December 7, 2022 deed, and the report the Board required

beats.text: The Board reappointed her in December 2024. Her term runs to 2027.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
